Map › Flow: Fulfilling a customer's order › Stage 1: Place the order › Process step 1.1: The customer's basket is emptied › Part: Ordering API

Part: Ordering API

The process steps that rely on it, and where it is measured exists proposed cannot be counted

  • Stage 1: Place the order: Process step 1.1: The customer's basket is emptied, Expected outcome: The order is placed
  • Stage 2: Accept the order: Process step 2.1: The order is released for stock checking when the grace period ends, Process step 2.2: Stock is confirmed for every item of the order, Expected outcome: Payment is taken for the order, Other outcome: The order is cancelled because an item is out of stock, Other outcome: The order is cancelled because payment failed, Other outcome: The order is cancelled at the customer's request
  • Stage 3: Ship the order: Process step 3.1: Stock is reduced by the order's units, Process step 3.2: Webhook subscribers are told the order is paid, Expected outcome: The order is shipped
  • Stage 4: Deliver the order: Process step 4.1: Webhook subscribers are told the order is shipped

What it is, what it depends on, where it sits

Kind
API service
Purpose
Owns the order: it creates it, moves it through every status, and publishes each change from its outbox as an integration event
Depends on
  • Ordering database (database)
  • Identity API (identity provider)
  • Event bus (message broker)
